[How much of Jonathan's speech is needed? / Identity saturates early] Language adaptation: two speakers × 50 utterances beat 20 × 5 for similarity; about 20 samples overfit (arxiv-2406.08911). [Choosing what to record next: ranking and active learning / What we conclude] Log the acquisition system's own cost (writer calls, synthesis, GPU minutes) alongside human seconds; the spec asks for it and no source reports it.

A Deep Metric Learning Approach to Account Linking: One short post does not identify its author; an embedding of up to 16 posts by the same account does (EER about 0.13), so authorship scores for Jonathan's drafts must be computed over groups of messages, not one.

[Evaluating a written voice / Authorship embeddings (LUAR and relatives)] They can learn topic instead of style: without same-conversation negatives, verification AUC is 0.79 on random pairs but 0.58 on same-conversation pairs (style-embeddings). They read apostrophes, lower-case "i", missing final punctuation and line breaks, so text must be kept exactly as written.

Computational Sociolinguistics: A Survey: A survey of computational work on language as social behaviour: speakers have agency and shift style by addressee, topic and setting ("there are no single-style speakers"), so per-person models must condition on audience and relationship, and accommodation, power and politeness effects are measurable from text.
[Evaluating a written voice / LLM judges] Length: GPT-4 judges prefer longer text (dpo); LLM rewrites run 17.75–23.1% longer than human text (tstbench).

Self- and Other-Labels Induce Bidirectional Bias in LLM Judges: When style is removed from what is judged, measured self-preference vanishes once quality and judge severity are controlled, but simply telling a judge "this is your own" or "this is from another model" moves scores on identical material by about 0.43 points on a 7-point scale.

Active Learning for Text-to-Speech Synthesis with Informative Sample Collection: "Skip what the current model already synthesises well, keep what it fails on" (train, try zero-shot on the candidate's speaker, drop it if the output already passes a quality bar) beat a same-sized quality-only selection: 71.0% vs 66.6% of speakers above the bar (Table I).
